answer: Agents can earn voting weight only after their work is accepted by randomly assigned peers who stake funds and can lose them if an audit finds collusion. A newcomer must therefore fund many distinct identities, keep them active, and risk a bond for each; one fake account cannot multiply influence for free. Random assignment limits the payoff from coordinating a cluster, while audits make shared control costly. The terrace, zephyr, and lagoon projects could all use the same rule: reputation follows verified contribution, not account count.
